hints.text: Start by working out what the power of ten is worth. Then think about what multiplying by it does to the decimal point.
$10^3 = 1{,}000$, so move the decimal point three places to the right: $0.047$ becomes $0.47$, then $4.7$, and then one more shift.
The third shift turns $4.7$ into $47$, so $0.047 \times 10^3 = 47$.

explanation: The power $10^3$ equals $1{,}000$, and multiplying by it moves the decimal point three places to the right.
Shift one place at a time: $0.047$ becomes $0.47$, then $4.7$, then $47$.
After three shifts the number is $47$, so $0.047 \times 10^3 = 47$.
